cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You beat me at chess. Leave the board exactly there; I'll take your photograph with the finishing move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you use your queen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may analyze my pieces later. I was exploring the rest of my team. Show me where you saw the finish.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you go easy on me? I want to know before we take the picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found that move without my help. Put your hand beside it and tell me how you spotted it. I'll take the picture when you're ready to explain your win.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls photo, A3 defers B2 queen analysis and directs finishing-move account, A5 responds to B4 doubt by deciding photo readiness through B explanation, protecting confidence by controlling attention.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 queen question causes A3 alternative-piece excuse; B4 picture objection causes A5 move demonstration before the photo.

relationship.evidence: B2 notices unused strength and B4 wants genuine achievement, a plausible winner concern A responds to with a concrete accomplishment.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 refusal of unearned celebration to put B own reasoning into the photograph, strengthening confidence without admitting the concession.

specificity.evidence: A1 chess board and final move, B2 queen give enough game context without requiring the entire position.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 hand beside move and explanation are practical actions rather than a detached compliment.
